applies_why: The judge text weighs a collision between the challenger's seed/loins chain and the defender's chain, which is the chain-against-chain case the rule governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse
room: the phrase 'by footing' had to be interpreted: one reading is grounding in the verses beneath and the links before (the DEFINITION's sense), the other is an explicit statement in the verses; I took the first, under which the judge's footed/rests-on-inference comparison is a footing weighing.
why: The judge compares the two chains by their footing (footed, but one rests on an inference) and never weighs verse by verse, so it obeys the rule.
